arxiv-2201-02563.title: Security Considerations for Virtual Reality Systems
arxiv-2201-02563.creator: Karthik Viswanathan 1, Abbas Yazdinejad 2
arxiv-2201-02563.description: Abstract There is a growing need for authentication methodology in virtual reality applications. Current systems assume that the immersive experience technology is a collection of peripheral devices connected to a personal computer or mobile device. Hence there is a complete reliance on the computing device with traditional authentication mechanisms to handle the authentication and authorization decisions.

arxiv-2210-12300.title: BEANS: The Benchmark of Animal Sounds
arxiv-2210-12300.creator: Masato Hagiwara, Benjamin Hoffman, Jen-Yu Liu, Maddie Cusimano
arxiv-2210-12300.description: Abstract The use of machine learning (ML) based techniques has become increasingly popular in the field of bioacoustics over the last years. Fundamental requirements for the successful application of ML based techniques are curated, agreed upon, high-quality datasets and benchmark tasks to be learned on a given dataset.

arxiv-2403-14403.title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
arxiv-2403-14403.creator: Soyeong Jeong, Jinheon Baek, Sukmin Cho, Sung Ju Hwang, Jong C. Park, School of Computing, Graduate School of AI, Korea Advanced Institute of Science, Technology {starsuzi,jinheon.baek,nelllpic,sjhwang82,jongpark}@kaist.ac.kr
arxiv-2403-14403.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Soyeong Jeong, Jinheon Baek, Sukmin Cho, Sung Ju Hwang, Jong C. Park, School of Computing, Graduate School of AI, Korea Advanced Institute of Science, Technology {starsuzi,jinheon.baek,nelllpic,sjhwang82,jongpark}@kaist.ac.kr. Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models (LLMs), which incorporate the non-parametric knowledge from external knowledge bases into LLMs, have emerged as a promising approach to enhancing response accuracy in several tasks, such as Question-Answering (QA).

arxiv-2505-22795.title: Window observables for benchmarking parton distribution functions
arxiv-2505-22795.creator: Joe Karpie, Christopher J. Monahan, Kostas Orginos, Savvas Zafeiropoulos
arxiv-2505-22795.description: Abstract Global analysis of collider and fixed-target experimental data and calculations from lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) are used to gain complementary information on the structure of hadrons. We propose novel “window observables” that allow for higher precision cross-validation between the different approaches, a critical step for studies that wish to combine the datasets.

arxiv-2508-12304.title: Adjustable AprilTags For Identity Secured Tasks
arxiv-2508-12304.creator: Hao Li
arxiv-2508-12304.description: Abstract Special tags such as AprilTags that facilitate image processing and pattern recognition are useful in practical applications. In close and private environments, identity security is unlikely to be an issue because all involved AprilTags can be completely regulated. However, in open and public environments, identity security is no longer an issue that can be neglected.

pmc-10480489.title: Entanglement in the quantum phases of an unfrustrated Rydberg atom array
pmc-10480489.creator: Matthew J. O’Rourke, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan
pmc-10480489.description: Recent experimental advances have stimulated interest in the use of large, two-dimensional arrays of Rydberg atoms as a platform for quantum information processing and to study exotic many-body quantum states. However, the native long-range interactions between the atoms complicate experimental analysis and precise theoretical understanding of these systems.

pmc-11436579.title: Reproducibility of [18F]MK-6240 kinetics in brain studies with shortened dynamic PET protocol in healthy/cognitively normal subjects
pmc-11436579.creator: Phelipi N Schuck, Xiuyuan H Wang, Emily B Tanzi, Sally Xie, Yi Li, Sadek A Nehmeh
pmc-11436579.description: Background[18F]MK-6240 is a neurofibrillary tangles PET radiotracer that has been broadly used in aging and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) studies. Majority of [18F]MK-6240 PET studies use dynamic acquisitions longer than 60 min to assess the tracer kinetic parameters. As of today, no consensus has been established on the optimum dynamic PET scan time.

pmc-11453642.title: 7680 Targeting HIF1α Enhances Exercise Benefits in High Fat Diet-Fed Mice
pmc-11453642.creator: J Yu, C Cheung, J E Gunton
pmc-11453642.description: Disclosure: J. Yu: None. C. Cheung: None. J.E. Gunton: None.Exercise is well-established to be beneficial for obesity, type 2 diabetes (T2D) and cardiovascular health. Exercise induces hypoxia inducible factor 1α (HIF1α) in muscle. HIF1α is well-known for its role in cell survival and adaptation, particularly in states of hypoxia.

pmc-11640011.title: Evaluation of Antioxidant and Antibacterial Activity of Gelatin Nanoparticles with Bitter Orange Peel Extract for Food Applications
pmc-11640011.creator: Adamaris García-Juárez, Alba Mery Garzón-García, José Rogelio Ramos-Enríquez, José Agustín Tapia-Hernández, Saúl Ruiz-Cruz, Dalila Fernanda Canizales-Rodríguez, Carmen Lizette Del-Toro-Sánchez, Francisco Rodríguez-Félix, Víctor Manuel Ocaño-Higuera, José de Jesús Ornelas-Paz
pmc-11640011.description: Bitter orange is a citrus fruit rich in bioactive compounds, but its waste is currently underutilized. One potential solution is to encapsulate these bioactive compounds. This research aims to synthesize gelatin nanoparticles loaded with an ethanolic extract of bitter orange peel and to evaluate their in vitro antioxidant and antibacterial activities.

pmc-12402153.title: New insights into the docking mechanism of vanillin on three mammalian olfactory receptors via a new statistical physics model
pmc-12402153.creator: Ismahene Ben Khemis, Fatma Aouaini, Salah Knani, Besma Graba, Nizar Lefi, Abdelmottaleb Ben Lamine
pmc-12402153.description: A new finite multi-layer model coupled with real gas law is successfully established using statistical physics theory and applied to theoretically characterize the docking process of vanillin key food odorant on human hOR8H1, chimpanzee cOR8H1, and horse hoOR8H1 olfactory receptors.

pmc-12466645.title: Dose-Dependent Effects of L-Serine Supplementation on Boar Sperm Quality During Chilled and Cryopreserved Storage
pmc-12466645.creator: Vibuntita Chankitisakul, Himalai Saiyamanon, Wuttigrai Boonkum, Eakapol Wangkahart, Ruthaiporn Ratchamak, Kampon Kaeoket, Panida Chanapiwat, Maria Grazia Palmerini
pmc-12466645.description: Simple SummaryMaintaining the quality of boar semen during storage is crucial for effective breeding programs. However, current storage methods, especially cooling and freezing, can damage sperm cells due to temperature stress and harmful molecules, such as reactive oxygen species. This study explored whether L-serine supplementation could protect boar sperm during chilled and cryopreserved storage.

pmc-13218070.title: Biocomputing: Beyond the Hype
pmc-13218070.creator: Simon Spichak, Kayleigh-Ann Clegg
pmc-13218070.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Biocomputing is a nascent but rapidly developing field at the intersection of biology and computer science. In this News and Perspectives article, JMIR Correspondent Simon Spichak reports on its current and potential applications for health care research and beyond.Keywords: brain organoids, cloud computing, human-machine systems, drug discovery, cognition, brain mapping, artificial intelligence, bioethics Key Takeaways: Biocomputing connects human brain organoids to a computer to see how they respond to electrical and chemical stimuli.

pmc-13242796.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIn the USA, higher forced vital capacity (FVC) is linked with longer survival, and FVC is associated with survival independently of ethnicity. The implications for the low FVC values in parts of Asia and Africa are unknown.MethodsWe used data from 16 sites of the multinational Burden of Obstructive Lung Disease (BOLD) study that completed follow-up of participants between 2019 and 2021 and reported at least five deaths between baseline and follow-up.

pmc-13452405.title: Phantoms for use in optical coherence elastography
pmc-13452405.creator: Farzan Navaeipour, Jiayue Li, Shima Zamani, Lena Kranold, Rowan W. Sanderson, Brendan F. Kennedy
pmc-13452405.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). .SignificanceOptical coherence elastography (OCE) is an emerging biomedical imaging technique for mapping the micro-scale mechanical properties of tissue. Phantoms are vital for assessing OCE imaging performance in a controlled and systematic manner.
